`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- A closed enumeration that feeds a SQLite CHECK is a contract, not documentation: every row must satisfy it, so a missing value (concrete-class callbacks, not-applicable roles) forces false data into the catalog rather than merely leaving a gap.
- Session termination semantics matter for reconnect loops: a 400 tells a client its request is malformed and it will typically retry the same thing, while a 404 is the signal the spec uses to make it re-initialize. Mixing them makes recovery behaviour unspecified.
- Copy-then-hash-then-open is the right order for content-URI imports because it removes the provider from the trust path, but SQLite schema objects (views, triggers) are executable, so file-level hashing alone does not make the database safe to query.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- A closed enumeration that feeds a SQLite CHECK is a contract, not documentation: every row must satisfy it, so a missing value (concrete-class callbacks, not-applicable roles) forces false data into the catalog rather than merely leaving a gap.
- Session termination semantics matter for reconnect loops: a 400 tells a client its request is malformed and it will typically retry the same thing, while a 404 is the signal the spec uses to make it re-initialize. Mixing them makes recovery behaviour unspecified.
- Copy-then-hash-then-open is the right order for content-URI imports because it removes the provider from the trust path, but SQLite schema objects (views, triggers) are executable, so file-level hashing alone does not make the database safe to query.
